title: Large Language Models and User Trust: Consequence of Self-Referential Learning Loop and the Deskilling of Healthcare Professionals

bias_targets.methodology: Conceptual analysis of how clinicians might exhibit undue trust in LLM outputs based on prior reliability, leading to the acceptance of AI suggestions without extensive verification.
Theoretical evaluation of human-AI interaction where clinicians may overlook or undervalue subsequent contradictory information if an LLM's recommendation aligns with their initial diagnosis.
Conceptual discussion of scenarios where a clinician doubts their own expertise during a disagreement with the AI, perceiving the LLM as the safer alternative for decision-making.
Theoretical examination of a feedback loop where LLMs are increasingly trained on AI-generated data, potentially amplifying data homogeneity and entrenching prevailing clinical biases and approaches.
